question: A 12-year-old boy is brought to the physician because of difficulty in walking for 5 months. His mother reports that he has trouble keeping his balance and walking without support. Over the past year, he has started to have difficulty seeing in the dark and his hearing has been impaired. Examination shows marked scaling of the skin on the face and feet and a shortened 4th toe. Muscle strength is 3/5 in the lower extremities and 4/5 in the upper extremities. Sensation to pinprick is symmetrically decreased over the legs. Fundoscopy shows peripheral pigment deposits and retinal atrophy. His serum phytanic acid concentration is markedly elevated. The patient's condition is most likely caused by a defect in which of the following cellular structures?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Peroxisomes -> Impaired phytanic acid metabolism -> Accumulation of phytanic acid -> Neurological symptoms and skin manifestations -> Defect in peroxisomes likely causing the patient's condition -> 95%
enhanced_information: The patient's condition is most likely caused by a defect in peroxisomes. Impaired phytanic acid metabolism leading to its accumulation results in neurological symptoms and skin manifestations. The association of skin manifestations with Staphylococcus aureus and lipids located in peroxisomes supports this conclusion.
analysis: The patient's presentation with neurological symptoms, skin manifestations, elevated phytanic acid concentration, and association with peroxisomes strongly suggests a defect in peroxisomes. Impaired phytanic acid metabolism due to this defect leads to the observed symptoms. Peroxisomes play a crucial role in phytanic acid metabolism, and their dysfunction can result in the clinical findings described.
